subject: Literature
title: Chaucer and the Rise of English Literature
description: A 60-second lesson on Chaucer and the Rise of English Literature.

hook.text: In fourteenth-century England, serious literature was written in French or Latin. English was for peasants.

buildup.text: Geoffrey Chaucer defied convention by writing The Canterbury Tales entirely in Middle English.

discovery.text: His pilgrims told bawdy, funny, and profound stories that captured every social class of medieval England.

twist.text: Chaucer never finished the Tales. He planned over a hundred stories but completed only twenty-four.

climax.text: By choosing English, Chaucer helped legitimize it as a literary language and shaped its future forever.

punchline.text: A peasant language became the tongue of Shakespeare.

quiz.question: Why was Chaucer's use of English controversial?
options: English was already the dominant literary language
Serious literature was written in French or Latin, not English
Chaucer could not read French or Latin
